t.E129.agn: In its 2009 re-evaluation EFSA did not change the acceptable daily intake (ADI); it stated that the limit may be exceeded only in some high-consuming children. EFSA stated that the available data, including the Southampton study, did not confirm a causal link between individual colours and behavioural effects; the EU nevertheless kept the warning label mandatory for products containing it.
t.E129.body: In rats and dogs, absorption of orally administered Allura red is limited; it is mainly excreted in faeces. No unchanged dye was measured in urine; the main product is cresidine sulphonic acid, formed when gut bacteria split the azo bond.
t.E129.eff.0.t: May have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children; in the EU this warning is mandatory on the label of products containing it. EFSA did not confirm a causal link with individual colours
t.E129.eff.1.t: The daily limit may be exceeded
t.E129.eval: In the EU, the labels of products containing this colour must carry the warning “may have an adverse effect on attention and activity in children” (following the 2007 Southampton study).
t.E129.prod: An azo dye produced by chemical synthesis.
t.E129.summary: A synthetic, red azo dye. It is used in confectionery, drinks and desserts.
